## Simple explanation

An AI agent is a software system that can take in information, decide what
to do, and use available actions or tools to make progress toward a goal.
Some agents use a language model to choose those actions.

## Technical explanation

An agent typically combines a policy or controller with observations,
available actions, and an execution environment. In model-based systems, a
language model may select tools or propose steps, while application code
handles permissions, validation, state, and execution. How much autonomy an
agent has depends on its design.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Agents can connect model capabilities to APIs, search, databases, and
business workflows. They also introduce risks such as incorrect tool use,
unbounded loops, and unintended side effects, so bounded permissions and
evaluation are essential.

## How it works

1. Receive a goal and relevant context.
2. Select a next step, which may be a tool call.
3. Execute the step and observe its result.
4. Continue, ask for clarification, or stop when the goal or stopping
   condition is reached.

## Practical example

A support agent might search an approved knowledge base, draft an answer,
and ask a human to approve it before sending. The approval step keeps the
agent from taking an external action on its own.

## Common misconceptions

- A chatbot is not necessarily an agent; it may only generate text.
- An agent is not necessarily fully autonomous.
- Adding tools does not by itself make a system reliable or safe.
